title: clear_model_cache(run_id=...) rmtree's a run's disk-cache directory without holding `_disk_cache_run_in_use` or the per-artifact I/O lock, violating the module's own eviction-safety invariant and racing a concurrent load of the same run
description: Every other disk-cache mutation in this module is serialized against in-flight loads: _evict_disk_cache snapshots `_active_disk_cache_runs()` and re-checks `_disk_cache_active_runs` under its guard before each rmtree (lines 589-602), and download/move/corrupt-retry-delete all run under `_artifact_io_lock(run_id, artifact_path)` wrapped in `_disk_cache_run_in_use(run_id)` (e.g. lines 911-918, 1016). clear_model_cache(run_id=...) does NOT participate in either mechanism: at lines 734-737 it computes `target = cache_root / run_id` and calls `shutil.rmtree(target, ignore_errors=True)` with no `_disk_cache_run_in_use` increment and no `_artifact_io_lock`. A concurrent load_mlflow_model for the same run can therefore observe `local_path.is_file()` True (line 643 or 917), then have the directory rmtree'd out from under it before load_local_model() opens the file, surfacing a spurious FileNotFoundError; or the loader's `cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` + `shutil.move` (lines 685-686) can interleave with the rmtree and leave a half-deleted run directory. Because rmtree uses ignore_errors=True the partial deletion is silent. Severity is low: clear_model_cache is operator-invoked, the load failure is recovered by _load_with_bounded_retry's re-download, and prices are never wrong — but it is a genuine inconsistency with the eviction-safety invariant the rest of the module is built around (the disk-eviction path went to lengths to be race-safe; the targeted clear bypasses all of it).
evidence: clear_model_cache run_id branch (lines 733-737): `target = cache_root / run_id; if target.exists(): removed = ...; shutil.rmtree(target, ignore_errors=True)` — no `with _disk_cache_run_in_use(run_id)` and no `with _artifact_io_lock(run_id, ...)` anywhere in the function (the only guarded access in the function is `_validate_disk_cache_run_id` at line 728 and the in-memory `_model_cache.evict_matching` at line 757). Contrast _evict_disk_cache (lines 589-602) which both excludes `_active_disk_cache_runs()` from candidates AND re-checks `if d.name in _disk_cache_active_runs: continue` under `_disk_cache_active_runs_guard` before rmtree, and the loader paths that hold `_artifact_io_lock` while touching the same files. No catalog/known finding covers clear_model_cache concurrency.
